sections.h2: Where is the Oxford recording office, and how do I phone it?
sections.html:
Go to the courthouse at 101 Main Street, Oxford, NC 27565, or call 919-693-6314. Letters go to P.O. Box 427 in the same city.

The county's online ordering page gives office hours as weekdays, 8:30 AM to 5 PM, and says a request sent after 4 PM waits until the next business day. For a sale, phone first and ask what the staff will need for your type of instrument, since they may not draft or repair documents.

The register of deeds is a countywide elected position, and G.S. 161-1 sets the term at two years.

sections.h2: Which documents does the Oxford office file?
sections.html:
Real estate records are the core of its work: deeds, deeds of trust, cancellations, plats, assumed names, powers of attorney and similar instruments. The county says each is recorded, indexed and scanned, and that deed records stretch back to 1746.

  • Land records: deeds, deeds of trust, plats and cancellations.
  • Personal records: births, deaths, marriages and marriage licenses.
  • Other filings: military discharges and notary commissions, plus the oath for Granville County notaries.

Staff run a recording counter, not a legal clinic. The office tells filers that state law bars it from practicing law, so it will not supply legal forms, coach you through filling one in, or say what a recorded document means legally. A North Carolina attorney can answer those questions.

sections.h2: What does Granville charge for vital records ordered online?
sections.html:
A certified birth, marriage or death certificate is $10.00 each, and an uncertified copy is $1.00, with a non-refundable $4 service and card fee on every online order. Records on the system begin in 1913.

Online vital record prices on the Granville County Register of Deeds ordering page (https://granvillecounty.org/731/Online-Ordering-Vital-Records)

A copy of a valid photo ID is required with every request. Anyone newly married should wait 10 days after the ceremony before ordering a certified marriage copy. Death certificates may also be picked up by a funeral director who shows license proof.

sections.h2: Which fees apply when a Granville County deed is filed?
sections.html:
Expect two charges on a sale: a recording fee set statewide and the seller's excise tax. G.S. 161-10 makes the fee identical in all counties.

  • General instruments: $26.00 through page 15, plus $4.00 for each page beyond that.
  • Mortgages and deeds of trust: $64.00 through page 35, plus $4.00 per page beyond that.
  • Cancellations of a deed of trust: nothing to record.

The tax is $1.00 per $500 of consideration or value, rounding any remainder up, and G.S. 105-228.30 puts it on the transferor, due before recording. The county keeps half. For a tract in several counties, the one with the most value collects it. Because the tax is figured from the stated consideration, make sure the deed reflects the real contract.

sections.h2: Why should a Granville County deed be recorded promptly?
sections.html:
An unrecorded deed does not bind later buyers or lien creditors. G.S. 47-18 gives priority to the instrument registered first, measured by time, in whichever county holds the land.

That rule covers leases over three years, options and rights of first refusal as well. Seller-financed deals fall under Chapter 47H, which tells the seller to record the contract or a Memorandum of a Contract for Deed inside five business days and gives the purchaser until midnight of the third business day to cancel.

sections.h2: Is there protection against property fraud in Granville County?
sections.html:
Yes. The register of deeds' office provides a free alert tool, PropertyCheck, through its software vendor. Owners can ask for an email or text whenever a document is recorded that matches a name, a street address or a parcel number.

  • Register on the vendor's website.
  • Create alerts for each version of your name and for your spouse.
  • Add the property address and parcel number.

The county describes the scheme it guards against: a forger moves title into another name and records the paperwork while the real owner stays unaware. An alert does not block a filing. It gives you the chance to call 919-693-6314 and consult a lawyer fast.

sections.h2: Who may collect a vital record in person at the Oxford office?
sections.html:
Anyone picking up a record must show valid state-issued photo ID, and the county limits who may collect it for someone else. Online requests are first come, first served, with no refunds, and all messages about an order arrive by email.

  • The person named on the record.
  • A spouse, brother or sister, parent or step-parent, grandparent, or child, step-child or grandchild.
  • A funeral director, for a death certificate only, with proof of license.
  • An authorized agent, attorney or legal representative, who may be asked for proof.

Inaccurate order details can stop a request from being processed. Requests are handled on business days during office hours, and the vendor's help address for the ordering tool is on the ordering page.

sections.h2: What should a Granville County seller check in the records before closing?
sections.html:
Look up your own parcel on the Register of Deeds' online records first. The county says documents are available online and that copies can be had on request, so a seller can pull the vesting deed and any old loan paperwork without a trip to the courthouse.

  • The deed that put the property in your name, matching spelling and legal description.
  • Any deed of trust that was paid off but never cancelled of record.
  • Plats or easements that affect the parcel.
  • Assumed-name filings, if a business ran from the house.

A cleanup before listing is usually faster than a cleanup under a closing deadline. Where a recorded instrument looks wrong, call the office at 919-693-6314 to find out how it can be corrected, and bring an attorney in for anything that needs legal drafting.

sections.h2: How does the Oxford recording counter connect to the county tax office?
sections.html:
They are separate offices with a shared subject. Recording moves title, while Granville County Tax Administration, at 919-693-4181, sets the value and bills the tax. Under G.S. 105-355 unpaid tax becomes a lien on the parcel as of the January 1 listing date, so the balance should be settled by the time a new deed is recorded.

The county offers a 1.5% discount on current taxes paid between July 1 and August 15, and the bill is due September 1. A seller who closes in that window can ask the tax office what a prompt payment would save. Oxford, Butner, Creedmoor, Stem and Stovall all sit in this one county, so a deed for land in any of them is recorded at the single courthouse counter in Oxford.

sections.h2: How many homes and households does Granville County have?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists 25,685 housing units in 2025 and 22,474 households across 2020 to 2024, averaging 2.52 residents each.

  • Veterans: 3,363.
  • Building permits in 2025: 257.
  • People living at the same address as a year earlier: 90.4%.
  • Midpoint monthly cost for owners paying a mortgage: $1,546.
  • Poverty rate: 13.5%.

These county figures give background on the market. Recording charges come from state law, so they stay the same whatever the numbers show.

faqs.q: What will a standard deed cost to file?
faqs.a: The base is $26.00 for the first 15 pages and $4.00 for each page after, as G.S. 161-10 sets it. The seller adds the excise tax, which is $1.00 per $500 of value.
The ordering page lists 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM, Monday to Friday. Call 919-693-6314 ahead of a visit for a deed that has unusual features.

faqs.q: Can staff prepare my deed for me?
faqs.a: No. The office is a recording office, and North Carolina law keeps its staff from practicing law, so it cannot supply forms or advise on legal effect. Hire an attorney for drafting.

faqs.q: Is a loan payoff cancellation free to record?
faqs.a: Yes. The state fee schedule lists no charge for a satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust or mortgage.

faqs.q: How far back do Granville deeds go?
faqs.a: The county page says deeds are available back to 1746, while vital records ordered online start in 1913.
